q: Which correctly compares NAD in respiration with NADP in photosynthesis?
options: NAD collects H from food and gives it to the ETC; NADP collects electrons from PSI for the Calvin cycle
Both are reduced only at the end of their electron transport chains, and both are then oxidised by O2
NADP is reduced in the Krebs cycle of mitochondria, while NAD is reduced by photosystem I in thylakoids
Both carry electrons from the Calvin cycle to the mitochondria, linking the two processes
explanation: Both are hydrogen/electron carriers that differ by one phosphate group. NAD works in catabolism: it collects hydrogen in glycolysis, the link reaction and Krebs, and delivers electrons to the respiratory ETC. NADP works in anabolism: it collects electrons at the end of the photosynthetic ETC (PSI → ferredoxin) and delivers them to the Calvin cycle to reduce GP.
